A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AgentAsk. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, figures and prompts, support comparison. Content can be matched across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports an original 824-log audit, five-benchmark evaluations, accuracy/latency/cost measurements, backbone and training-stage ablations, and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds reward-component ablations, PPO/GRPO comparisons, and an additional decoding-temperature/seed evaluation.

M1.justification: v2 revises the described E-GRPO rule to progressively increase global-credit weights and explicitly sets A_loc = r_edge; Algorithm 1 drops v1's G-candidate sampling instruction. The prompt also broadens recipients beyond sender/receiver, although Appendix A.2 retains that restriction. These are limited procedural revisions within the retained architecture; the precise weighting schedule remains unspecified.

E1.justification: Both versions use GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval, MMLU and MBPP, alongside the 824-log audit. Transfer from training on one framework to other frameworks was already reported in v1 Appendix C. Added decoding and reward configurations do not introduce new task or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Self-Refine becomes an evaluated baseline in the main comparison, having previously appeared only in discussion. v2 Table 9 also introduces reported PPO and GRPO comparisons across four frameworks and five benchmarks. These substantially broaden comparisons beyond the retained prompting, framework and clarifier baselines.

E3.justification: v2 Appendix C.1 adds evaluation at temperature 0.3, whereas v1 explicitly specified temperature 0. New reward-removal and terminal-only conditions support the added controlled experiments. The benchmark metrics and executor/backbone choices remain; v2 does not specify the default temperature underlying its revised main results.

E4.justification: v2 adds reward-component and terminal-only ablations (Tables 3 and 8), optimizer comparisons (Table 9), decoding robustness results (Table 4), and dataset-wise edge-resolution results. Existing backbone/SFT comparisons, parameter sensitivity analysis and four-type case studies are retained or relocated, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v2 first reports standard deviations for the improved settings in Table 1, quantifies annotation agreement with Fleiss' kappa of 0.84, and identifies seed 1314 for Appendix C.1. v1 provides point results and qualitative agreement statements. v2 does not specify the run count or runs underlying its standard deviations.

E6.justification: Results change extensively: AgentAsk's GPTSwarm/MATH score changes from 51.29 to 55.05, and its Qwen/E-GRPO MasRouter/GSM8K accuracy, normalized latency and extra cost change from 94.72/103/4.2 to 94.86/108/4.9. Reported DG one-shot resolution changes from 72.5% to 82.5%. New baseline, ablation and robustness results are added. These are revised reported outcomes, not established same-training performance gains.

T1.justification: Most equations are preserved or moved to Appendix A. Limited formulation changes include explicitly equating local advantage with edge reward and introducing time-varying global-credit weighting in Section 4.3. Neither version supplies theoretical proofs or guarantees.

C1.justification: The taxonomy and lightweight edge-clarification contributions remain. The headline overhead claim changes from below 5% to below 10%, and v2 introduces an accuracy-improvement claim of up to 4.69%. These revise the claimed accuracy-efficiency trade-off without redefining the central research contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations about gradual global credit avoiding local optima and interprets the new ablations as evidence that each reward component is necessary. Its limitations replace teacher/backbone dependence with a stronger applicability boundary concerning intrinsic agent hallucinations and inconsistencies; RD/CG difficulty is also newly attributed to hallucinations.

D1.justification: v2 adds annotator qualifications and a note about framework-specific prompt inputs, while retaining the same code link. It removes v1's explicit MasRouter training-source disclosure, temperature-0 statement, and defaults H=3 and lambda_sw=0.4. Most controller and SFT details are relocated, not newly disclosed.

R1.justification: v2 adds Gittell's relational-coordination work as conceptual grounding for the taxonomy and removes the SciAgents and chemistry-tool application references. Positioning relative to global orchestration, self-correction and clarification research is largely retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method exposition, experimental discussion and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Detailed modeling moves to Appendix A, three research questions become four, and the appendices are reorganized with a contents list and notation section. This substantially changes the narrative and navigation.

P2.justification: Table 1 is redesigned to display standard deviations and average gains. New robustness, reward-ablation, optimizer-comparison and notation tables are added. Figure 4 gains a resolution-rate radar panel, the sensitivity plot moves to Figure 5, and appendix displays are extensively relocated. The existing case-study tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful controls, comparisons, uncertainty statistics and clearer organization. However, revised evidence is inconsistently reconciled: Figure 4 retains v1's AgentAsk efficiency point of 103/4.2 while Table 2 reports 108/4.9; the headline 4.69% gain matches +GPT-5 in Table 1; and appendix latency values exceed the claimed 10% overhead ceiling. Run counts remain unspecified. These material reporting problems coexist with substantive evidential additions, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
